intro: Ahmedabad has seven zones on NXTutors, divided by the Sabarmati. On the west bank, Navrangpura, Paldi and Ellisbridge are the older heart of the western city, with low-rise blocks, independent houses and newer towers; Satellite, Vastrapur, Bodakdev and Thaltej line SG Highway with apartment complexes, bungalows and gated towers; and Prahlad Nagar, Bopal and Shela are the newer south-western corridor of modern gated complexes. On the east bank, Maninagar and Kankaria, Nikol and Naroda, and Shahibaug and Asarwa mix older houses on busy lanes, former mill chawls and mid-rise flats. Gated towers often log a visitor's phone number; older homes open onto the lane.

The Blue and Red Lines cross at Old High Court, so tutors from the northern suburbs or the east bank can ride into the western core and finish with a short auto trip or a walk. The Red Line runs north through Naranpura and Sabarmati to Motera Stadium, where the Gandhinagar line begins, and the Blue Line runs east to Vastral Gam and west to Thaltej Gam. Satellite, Vastrapur, Gota, Ghatlodia and the whole Bopal and Shela corridor have no station, so BRTS, city buses and two-wheelers fill the gap. The roads to the bridges, SG Highway service lanes and ring-road junctions slow down at office hours.

GSEB, the Gujarat board, is taught in Gujarati, English and other media, so families give board, class and medium together, and a tutor should be clear about the language they teach in. CBSE, ICSE and ISC are also followed, and a smaller group take the IB Diploma or Cambridge IGCSE. In Bopal and Shela, families often pair a nearby home tutor for core subjects with online lessons for specialist ones, and online teaching widens the choice for IB, IGCSE and advanced senior papers across the city. Mid-January's Uttarayan is a time to agree lesson changes in advance.

zone_notes.Navrangpura, Paldi & Ellisbridge: Old High Court links the Blue and Red Lines, and Red Line stops at Paldi, Ellisbridge and APMC let tutors from the north or east bank ride in. Apartment buildings want your name with the watchman before the first visit, independent houses need a lane and landmark, and roads towards the bridges are slowest at office hours.
zone_notes.Satellite, Vastrapur & Bodakdev: Thaltej Gam, Thaltej, Doordarshan Kendra and Gurukul Road stations serve the northern half, but Satellite, Jodhpur and Vastrapur have no station, so most tutors come by two-wheeler, auto or BRTS. Towers along SG Highway often log a visitor's phone number at the gate, and the service lanes thicken in the evening rush.
zone_notes.Prahlad Nagar, Bopal & Shela: No metro station serves this corridor, so tutors who already live in Bopal, South Bopal or Shela keep weekly slots most easily, and a ride from across the river is hard to repeat. Township-style complexes may check you at the main gate and again at the tower, so allow extra time for the first visit and avoid ring-road junctions at office hours.
zone_notes.Naranpura, Gota & Chandkheda: The Red Line runs through this zone from Vijay Nagar to Motera Stadium, and the Gandhinagar line means tutors from the capital can reach Chandkheda and Sabarmati by metro. Gota and Ghatlodia have no station, so a two-wheeler on your side of SG Highway is the practical way in, and Vijay Char Rasta crowds up in the evening.
zone_notes.Maninagar, Isanpur & Kankaria: Maninagar railway station, Kankaria East on the Blue Line and Apparel Park bring tutors in by train, metro or BRTS, and low-rise blocks usually mean a quick call from the entrance before you go up. Sundays, holidays and the December carnival crowd the lake area, and market roads near Maninagar station fill in the evening.
zone_notes.Nikol, Naroda & Bapunagar: Vastral, Amraiwadi and parts of Nikol sit on the Blue Line, while Bapunagar and old Naroda are doorstep visits in narrow lanes where a two-wheeler is far more practical than a car. Industrial shift times load the roads around Odhav and Naroda, so agree a fixed mid-evening lesson that avoids them.
zone_notes.Shahibaug, Asarwa & Meghaninagar: Shahibaug apartment buildings usually confirm each visitor with a call to the flat, while older homes in Asarwa and Meghaninagar open onto the lane. The nearest metro stops are Shahpur, Gheekanta and Kalupur, so most tutors come by road, and traffic near the medical campuses in Asarwa stays heavy through the day.

boards: Ahmedabad tutors teach GSEB, the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, which sets the SSC at the end of Standard 10 and separate HSC Science and HSC General exams at the end of Standard 12, alongside CBSE, ICSE and ISC, the IB and Cambridge IGCSE. GSEB's Standard 10 papers open with 24 compulsory one-mark items, and HSC Science papers begin with 50 multiple-choice questions on an OMR sheet. Read designs, question banks and results on gseb.org and the board's e-service site, CBSE material on cbseacademic.nic.in and CISCE documents on cisce.org.
faqs: How do Ahmedabad families get matched with me?

A parent sends a request with the class, board and medium, subjects, area and timings. NXTutors chooses two or three tutors starting with those living in that area, then those who travel there, then the zone, Ahmedabad and online. The family sees each shortlisted tutor's fee and books a free demo before deciding.
Can I teach online from Ahmedabad?

Yes. Online is a separate choice on your profile, and online requests are matched on subject, board, class and your free hours, not your address. You might teach GSEB or CBSE students across Gujarat online in the evening while keeping home classes on your own side of the Sabarmati.
Which side of the river should I cover?

Usually your own. Crossing the Sabarmati at office hours is slow, so list the zones on your bank first, then add the other side only if a metro line, such as the Red Line through Old High Court, takes you there directly. Bopal and Shela suit tutors who already live in that corridor.
What ID check do Ahmedabad tutors go through?

The same as every tutor who joins: you confirm your phone or email with a one-time code and upload a government photo ID, which our team reviews before your profile goes live. It is not a police check. Real tutors who pass display a Verified badge; How we verify tutors (/how-we-verify-tutors) covers the details.
Do tutors pay anything, and who sets the fee?

Tutor plans are paid; the Pricing page (/pricing) lists what each includes. You decide your own lesson fee, shown to Ahmedabad families before the free demo. A family can switch tutor without any charge, so a well-planned first demo and a slot you keep every week matter more than anything else.
